verdict.rationale: Meilisearch documents built-in ranking rules, including a "sort" rule, whose order developers can change. Its pricing page advertises Dynamic Search Rules to boost, pin, or bury results per request, so relevance shaping beyond text matching exists in part. The evidence never shows custom attribute-based ranking rules for popularity or margin signals, and a community user reports there are no decay functions for recency, which Elasticsearch supports. missing for 10: documented custom ranking rules on numeric business attributes (popularity, margin), recency/decay scoring, in-depth docs for Dynamic Search Rules beyond a pricing-page mention, hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can shape relevance with custom ranking rules and business signals (popularity, recency, margin) beyond textual matching

citations.quote: Meilisearch contains seven built-in ranking rules in the following order: ["words", "typo", "proximity", "attributeRank", "sort", "wordPosition", "exactness"]
Depending on your needs, you might want to change this order.
Dynamic Search Rules ... Boost, pin, or bury results based on the context of each request
